quote: Give me Books, fruit, French wine and fine weather and a little music out of doors, played by somebody I do not know.
source: John Keats, Letters of John Keats to His Family and Friends, letter CXIII to Fanny Keats, 28 August 1819 (ed. Sidney Colvin, 1891)
note: The circulating wording reorders the list and rewrites the clause. Colvin’s edition reads Books, fruit, French wine, and then a little music out of doors, played by somebody I do not know. That wording is restored here. The sentence runs on after know, so the closing full stop is the card’s.

evidence.where: Colvin’s edition read in full text, letter CXIII located and the passage read in place
evidence.edition: Letters of John Keats to His Family and Friends, ed. Sidney Colvin, 1891
evidence.locator: letter CXIII, To Fanny Keats, Winchester, August 28 [1819]

reason: The letter is genuine and correctly dated, but the proposed wording is a modern rearrangement. Colvin prints Give me Books, fruit, French wine and fine weather and a little music out of doors, played by somebody I do not know, and the sentence continues past that point.
